TriggerGroup.name: Mudlet base UI chat capture
TriggerGroup.script: -- A gate, then the shapes - the pattern to copy for triggers that have to -- watch every line. Each gate matches substrings, no regex engine, and Mudlet -- only offers a line to a trigger's children once its own pattern matched. A -- trigger with no pattern, like this folder, passes everything through. -- -- Substring patterns are case-sensitive, so every literal a child's regex -- needs must appear in its gate's pattern list, spelled the same way. Miss -- that and the child silently never sees a line. -- -- It is also why the gates spell out "says" and "You say" rather than the -- "say" they share: a gate hit costs a capture list and a script call before -- any child regex runs, and "say" would hand all that to every "essay". -- The channel gate cannot be narrowed like that, since a bare "[", "(" or -- "<" is all a tagged line has in common. -- -- This folder ships inactive and is the only thing the "Mudlet base UI" -- script switches: it enables the folder on load and disables it again when -- the game turns out to send its chat over GMCP. Nothing reaches a gate while -- the folder is off, so one switch retires the whole layer.

Script.name: Mudlet base UI
Script.script:
-- Mudlet base UI: a small starter interface that adapts to whatever the game -- provides. Nothing is created until the game actually sends something: -- vitals gauges are built from GMCP character data (normalised across the -- dialects games speak, and only for the fields that exist), with the map and -- chat windows alongside them. Chat comes from gmcp.Comm.Channel.Text when -- the game offers it; for everything else, additive triggers capture the -- common chat-line shapes (tells, says, channels) shared by most games - so -- on a game with no GMCP at all the UI appears on the first chat line. -- Chat is sorted into All/Tells/Channels tabs, and the map pane shows a -- placeholder until the profile actually has map data. -- Gauges have their own fallback ladder when GMCP is missing: MSDP is -- negotiated quietly, self-sufficient prompt lines (labelled cur/max or -- percent) are trusted once they recur, score screens are read passively, -- and as a last resort "score" is sent once - visibly - to learn the maxima -- on games whose prompt only carries current values. -- Every section starts in the dock but none is stuck there: dragging a header -- row pulls that section out to sit anywhere over the game's text, the sections -- left behind share out the space it had, and where each one was left is -- remembered between sessions. -- Type "baseui" for options; "baseui hide" removes it until "baseui show". BaseUI = BaseUI or {} BaseUI.sections = BaseUI.sections or {} BaseUI.gauges = BaseUI.gauges or {} BaseUI.usedGaugeSlots = BaseUI.usedGaugeSlots or 0 BaseUI.recentCaptures = BaseUI.recentCaptures or {} BaseUI.vitalsTriggerIds = BaseUI.vitalsTriggerIds or {} BaseUI.shapeSightings = BaseUI.shapeSightings or {} BaseUI.vitalsData = BaseUI.vitalsData or {} BaseUI.vitalsLock = BaseUI.vitalsLock or 0 BaseUI.eventHandlerIds = BaseUI.eventHandlerIds or {} -- An anonymous event handler belongs to the profile rather than to the package -- that registered it, so uninstalling has to take these with it. Every -- registration goes through here, including the ones made later in a session. -- The id is only recorded once: re-running this script (saving it in the editor -- does) hands back the ids registered the first time rather than new ones. local function onEvent(event, handler, oneShot) local id = registerAnonymousEventHandler(event, handler, oneShot) if not table.contains(BaseUI.eventHandlerIds, id) then BaseUI.eventHandlerIds[#BaseUI.eventHandlerIds + 1] = id end return id end local settingsFile = getMudletHomeDir() .. "/base_ui_settings.lua" local ownPackage = "mudlet-base-ui" -- Everything a look decides lives in one of these tables: the dock's chrome, -- the gauge colours, the font, and the colour the game's own text sits on. In -- all three the accent at full strength appears only on section headers and the -- active chat tab so it stays an accent; two of them reuse it heavily faded as the -- hover for a button. -- Fonts are limited to the families Mudlet ships, so a look's typography renders the -- same on a machine with nothing else installed. The two glyphs used as furniture -- (the palette button and the header grip) are in none of them and fall back per -- glyph, as the grip already did before any of this. local themes = { midnight = { label = "Midnight", blurb = "cool slate and cyan", accent = "#4fc1e9", bg = "#1b1e23", panel = "#14171c", border = "#3a4149", borderSoft = "#2b3138", text = "#e8eef4", textDim = "#96a0ab", font = "Ubuntu", hover = "rgba(90,100,110,50%)", tabActive = "#2b323b", tabInactive = "#1f242a", gaugeBack = "#2c313a", gauges = { hp = "#2f9e3f", mp = "#2f6f9e", xp = "#c28f2c", mv = "#2f9e8a", enemy = "#b23a3a" }, -- black, which is Mudlet's own default: this look asks for no tint at all console = nil, }, ember = { label = "Ember", blurb = "warm firelit fantasy", accent = "#e2703a", bg = "#191310", panel = "#0f0b09", border = "#4a3527", borderSoft = "#2e231b", text = "#ddd3c6", textDim = "#8d7f70", font = "Bitstream Vera Serif", hover = "rgba(226,112,58,22%)", tabActive = "#2a201a", tabInactive = "#17120f", gaugeBack = "#2a201a", gauges = { hp = "#c0452b", mp = "#7a4a9e", xp = "#c9962e", mv = "#7f9153", enemy = "#8e2f3a" }, console = { 18, 13, 11 }, }, hardlight = { label = "Hardlight", blurb = "cold instrument sci-fi", accent = "#8f7bff", bg = "#111420", panel = "#090b12", border = "#2f3559", borderSoft = "#1d2236", text = "#e6ebff", textDim = "#8a93b8", font = "Ubuntu Condensed", hover = "rgba(143,123,255,22%)", tabActive = "#1d2236", tabInactive = "#12151f", gaugeBack = "#1e2338", gauges = { hp = "#17c3a2", mp = "#7a6cff", xp = "#cfc23f", mv = "#3aa8e0", enemy = "#ff4d6d" }, console = { 9, 11, 20 }, }, } -- The order the palette button cycles through, which is also the order the "baseui" -- listing reads in. A look missing from here cannot be reached by the button at all. -- Names double as "baseui " keywords, so they go through the alias last. local themeOrder = { "midnight", "ember", "hardlight" } local defaultThemeName = "midnight" -- the look in force, a shallow copy of one of the above - so its gauges and -- console tables are still the look's own and must not be written to local theme = {} local layout = { -- Every section of the dock is a container of its own, and what a drag can -- take hold of is the strip of its background label its contents do not -- cover - so each one keeps a header row of this many pixels above them. -- Geyser resizes rather than moves on the top four pixel rows of that strip, -- on its leftmost eleven pixels and its rightmost ten; the rest of the row is -- what a drag can land on. Adjustable leaves twice its padding above its -- contents, so the padding is half of this. header = 20, -- what the dock gives each section as a share of its height, and the gap -- under it. The vitals panel has no height here: its bars decide that. map = { height = 0.37, gap = 0.015 }, chat = { height = 0.375, gap = 0.02 }, vitals = { gap = 0 }, -- where the sections end when the vitals panel is not in the dock to end them floor = 0.98, -- pixels rather than shares, unlike the sections: the chat section's tab row -- and the gap under it tabs = 20, tabGap = 4, } -- where the bars start, which is everything the dock hands out above them layout.barsTop = layout.map.height + layout.map.gap + layout.chat.height + layout.chat.gap -- top to bottom, which is also the order a section is put back into when it -- comes back to the dock local sectionOrder = { "map", "chat", "vitals" } local sectionTitles = { map = "MAP", chat = "CHAT", vitals = "VITALS" } -- what a section is called in the sentences the player reads local sectionNames = { map = "map", chat = "chat window", vitals = "health bars" } -- a grip in front of the title, so a header row reads as something to take hold -- of rather than as a caption local function sectionTitle(key) return string.format([[☰ %s]], theme.textDim, sectionTitles[key]) end -- every gauge is styled the same way, a thin HUD line: bold value text floating -- over a transparent zone, with a slim stat-colored line along the bottom -- 30% tracking the value. The band edge is a hard gradient stop - Qt -- gradient stops don't alpha-composite, so each band is either fully -- transparent or fully opaque local function gaugeStyle(color) return string.format( [[background-color: qlineargradient(x1:0, y1:0, x2:0, y2:1, stop:0 rgba(0,0,0,0), stop:0.6999 rgba(0,0,0,0), stop:0.70 %s, stop:1 %s); border: none;]], color, color) end -- A section's own background when it is out of the dock. In the dock only its -- header row shows, over the dock's own background; out of the dock it needs a -- background of its own, since a section may be part transparent and would -- otherwise be read against whatever game text happens to be behind it. The -- alignment is what keeps the title in the header row rather than centred over -- the section's contents. Docked needs no colour, so it is the one piece of -- section styling a look does not touch. local dockedSectionCss = [[background-color: transparent; border: 0px; padding-left: 2px; qproperty-alignment: 'AlignLeft | AlignTop';]] -- the text label spans the whole gauge; the padding floats the value text -- above the line, inset from the left edge local gaugeText = [[background-color: transparent; padding-left: 8px; padding-bottom: 9px;]] -- Written as the character rather than as an HTML entity because it goes into -- console text as well as into a label, and cecho prints an entity literally. local paletteGlyph = "◐" local mapPlaceholderText = "Your map will appear
here as you explore" -- Every stylesheet the dock paints with, rebuilt from `theme` whenever the look -- changes; the widgets are then repainted from here. local css = {} local gaugeDefs = { hp = {}, mp = {}, xp = {}, mv = {}, enemy = {} } local function rebuildCss() css.placeholder = string.format( [[background-color: %s; border: 1px solid %s; border-radius: 6px;]], theme.panel, theme.borderSoft) css.sectionFloating = string.format( [[background-color: %s; border: 1px solid %s; border-radius: 6px; padding-left: 2px; qproperty-alignment: 'AlignLeft | AlignTop';]], theme.bg, theme.border) -- the line closing off a header row. It sits on the row's own bottom pixel, so -- it is click-through and takes none of the strip a drag has to land on. css.headerRule = string.format([[background-color: %s; border: 0px;]], theme.borderSoft) css.button = string.format( [[QLabel{ border-color: %s; background-color: %s; } QLabel::hover{ background-color: %s; }]], theme.border, theme.bg, theme.hover) css.dock = string.format("background-color: %s; border: 1px solid %s;", theme.bg, theme.border) css.tabActive = string.format( [[background-color: %s; border: 1px solid %s; border-bottom: 2px solid %s; border-top-left-radius: 4px; border-top-right-radius: 4px;]], theme.tabActive, theme.border, theme.accent) css.tabInactive = string.format( [[background-color: %s; border: 1px solid %s; border-bottom: 2px solid %s; border-top-left-radius: 4px; border-top-right-radius: 4px;]], theme.tabInactive, theme.borderSoft, theme.borderSoft) css.gaugeBack = gaugeStyle(theme.gaugeBack) for key, color in pairs(theme.gauges) do gaugeDefs[key].front = gaugeStyle(color) end end -- GMCP vitals arrive in several dialects: lowercase namespaces, maxima inside -- the vitals message or in a separate Maxstats one, and varying key names. -- Every node listed here is scanned on each update (the gmcp table keeps the -- latest message per node, so currents and maxima merge naturally even when -- they arrive separately) - supporting another dialect is one more line local vitalsNodes = { { "Char", "Vitals" }, { "char", "vitals" }, { "Char", "Maxstats" }, { "char", "maxstats" }, { "Char", "Status" }, { "char", "status" }, } -- one row per gauge; current/max/percent list every key spelling observed in -- the wild. A percent key is a ready 0-100 value and needs no max: nl (IRE -- next-level percent) and tnlpct for xp, opponent_hp_pct and enemypct for -- enemy health. transient rows hide their gauge when the value goes away -- (the enemy died or was cleared). local vitalsStats = { { key = "hp", label = "HP", current = { "hp", "health" }, max = { "maxhp", "max_hp", "maxHp", "maxhealth", "max_health", "maxHealth" } }, { key = "mp", label = "MP", current = { "mp", "mana", "sp", "energy" }, max = { "maxmp", "max_mp", "maxMp", "maxmana", "max_mana", "maxMana", "maxsp", "max_sp", "maxSp", "maxenergy", "max_energy", "maxEnergy" } }, { key = "xp", label = "XP", percent = { "nl", "tnlpct" }, current = { "xp", "experience" }, max = { "maxxp", "max_xp", "maxXp", "maxexperience", "max_experience", "maxExperience" } }, { key = "enemy", label = "Enemy", transient = true, percent = { "opponent_hp_pct", "enemypct" } }, -- last on purpose: when a game supplies more stats than there are gauge -- slots, movement is the one to lose out { key = "mv", label = "MV", current = { "mv", "moves", "movement" }, max = { "maxmv", "max_mv", "maxMv", "maxmoves", "max_moves", "maxMoves", "maxmovement", "max_movement", "maxMovement" } }, } -- vitals can also come from MSDP or from prompt/score lines. A source lock -- keeps them from fighting: the first source to produce a complete hp -- reading owns the gauges, and only a higher-ranked source can take them -- over - so gauges built from a prompt hand themselves to GMCP whenever it -- turns up, however late local sourceRanks = { gmcp = 3, msdp = 2, prompt = 1 } -- the vitalsStats rows again, keyed by the conventional MSDP variable names local msdpStats = { { key = "hp", current = "HEALTH", max = "HEALTH_MAX" }, { key = "mp", current = "MANA", max = "MANA_MAX" }, { key = "xp", current = "EXPERIENCE", max = "EXPERIENCE_MAX" }, { key = "mv", current = "MOVEMENT", max = "MOVEMENT_MAX" }, { key = "enemy", current = "OPPONENT_HEALTH", max = "OPPONENT_HEALTH_MAX", transient = true }, } local function gmcpNode(path) local node = gmcp for _, key in ipairs(path) do if type(node) ~= "table" then return nil end node = node[key] end if type(node) == "table" then return node end end -- some games send numbers as strings, hence the tonumber()s; nested -- cur/max tables (vitals.hp = { cur = 10, max = 20 }) are handled too local function statReading(sources, stat) local current, max, percent for _, source in ipairs(sources) do for _, name in ipairs(stat.percent or {}) do percent = percent or tonumber(source[name]) end for _, name in ipairs(stat.current or {}) do local value = source[name] if type(value) == "table" then current = current or tonumber(value.cur) max = max or tonumber(value.max) else current = current or tonumber(value) end end for _, name in ipairs(stat.max or {}) do max = max or tonumber(source[name]) end end return current, max, percent end -- generic chat capture for games without GMCP chat: trigger shapes most games -- share. Capture is additive - the matched line is copied into the chat window -- with its colours and never removed from the main one. -- a "[tag]", "(tag)" or "< tag |" prefix only counts as chat when its first -- word is a well-known channel name - extend this list to cover more games BaseUI.chatChannelNames = { chat = true, say = true, tell = true, tells = true, gtell = true, newbie = true, newbies = true, gossip = true, grats = true, gratz = true, congrats = true, ooc = true, ic = true, clan = true, guild = true, order = true, house = true, city = true, market = true, auction = true, trade = true, talk = true, ask = true, answer = true, question = true, questions = true, music = true, quote = true, roleplay = true, rp = true, imm = true, group = true, party = true, team = true, shout = true, yell = true, form = true, town = true, } -- The same shapes as the "Mudlet base UI chat capture" trigger tree, in the -- same order (StarterUiTriggerCostTest compares them index by index): the tree -- routes chat, this copy tells the vitals layer which lines are conversation. -- tagged = true means the shape captures a channel tag that must pass the -- list above. local chatPatterns = { { regex = [=[^\w[\w'-]* tells you\b[^,:]{0,30}(?::|,?\s*['"])]=] }, { regex = [=[^You tell [\w'-]+[^,:]{0,30}(?::|,?\s*['"])]=] }, { regex = [=[^You tell the (?:group|formation)\b]=] }, { regex = [=[^\w[\w'-]* whispers to you\b[^,:]{0,30}(?::|,?\s*['"])]=] }, { regex = [=[^\w[\w'-]* tells the (?:group|formation)\b]=] }, { regex = [=[^You gossip[^,:]{0,20}(?::|,?\s*['"])]=] }, { regex = [=[^\w[\w'-]* (?:says|asks|exclaims)[^,:]{0,20},?\s*['"]]=] }, { regex = [=[^You (?:say|ask|exclaim)[^,:]{0,20},?\s*['"]]=] }, { regex = [=[^\w[\w'-]* (?:yells|shouts)[^,:]{0,20},?\s*['"]]=] }, { regex = [=[^You (?:yell|shout)[^,:]{0,20},?\s*['"]]=] }, { regex = [=[^\w[\w'-]* chats[^,:]{0,20},?\s*['"]]=] }, { regex = [=[^You chat[^,:]{0,20},?\s*['"]]=] }, { regex = [=[^\[([\w][\w -]{0,18})\]]=], tagged = true }, { regex = [=[^\(([\w -]{1,18})\)[:\s]]=], tagged = true }, { regex = [=[^< ?([\w -]{1,18}) ?\|]=], tagged = true }, } local chatTabs = { { key = "all", label = "All" }, { key = "tells", label = "Tells" }, { key = "channels", label = "Channels" }, } function BaseUI.routeChatLine(family) if BaseUI.gmcpChat or BaseUI.dormant() then return end -- several shapes can match the same line - copy it only once local lineNumber = getLineNumber() if lineNumber == BaseUI.lastChatLine then return end BaseUI.lastChatLine = lineNumber selectCurrentLine() copy() deselect() local firstBuild = not BaseUI.container BaseUI.build() if firstBuild then -- building resizes the main window, which can renumber lines; refresh the -- marker so other patterns matching this same line stay deduplicated BaseUI.lastChatLine = getLineNumber() end if not BaseUI.chats then return end BaseUI.chats.all:appendBuffer() BaseUI.noteChatActivity("all") if family and BaseUI.chats[family] then BaseUI.chats[family]:appendBuffer() BaseUI.noteChatActivity(family) end BaseUI.checkMapData() table.insert(BaseUI.recentCaptures, { text = line, time = getEpoch() }) if #BaseUI.recentCaptures > 10 then table.remove(BaseUI.recentCaptures, 1) end end function BaseUI.routeTaggedChatLine(tag) tag = type(tag) == "string" and tag:match("(%S+)") if not tag then return end tag = tag:lower() if not BaseUI.chatChannelNames[tag] then return end local family = (tag == "tell" or tag == "tells" or tag == "gtell") and "tells" or "channels" BaseUI.routeChatLine(family) end -- renaming these in the trigger tree means renaming them here local chatTree = "Mudlet base UI chat capture" local chatGates = { "BaseUI chat: tells", "BaseUI chat: speech", "BaseUI chat: channel tags" } -- a gate reached through a switched-off folder is not armed whatever its own -- flag says, and enableTrigger() only reports that it found the name - hence -- the ancestor check local function gateArmed(gate) return isActive(gate, "trigger", true) > 0 end -- enableTrigger and disableTrigger can only name a trigger, and a name is not -- unique: copying this tree in the editor reproduces every name exactly, so -- switching ours would switch the player's copy too. Only the folder is ever -- named here, which keeps a copied gate out of it, and when the folder name -- itself is shared the layer stops switching altogether - routeChatLine() -- re-checks gmcpChat and dormant() on every line, so what is captured stays -- right either way. All that is lost is the scans disarming would have saved. function BaseUI.chatTreeShared() return exists(chatTree, "trigger") ~= 1 end function BaseUI.armChatTriggers() if BaseUI.dormant() or BaseUI.gmcpChat then return end if BaseUI.chatTreeShared() then BaseUI.reportSharedChatTree() return end enableTrigger(chatTree) for _, gate in ipairs(chatGates) do if not gateArmed(gate) then BaseUI.reportDeadChatGate(gate) end end end function BaseUI.reportSharedChatTree() if BaseUI.warnedSharedChatTree then return end BaseUI.warnedSharedChatTree = true debugc("[ Mudlet UI ] more than one trigger is called \"" .. chatTree .. "\", so the chat capture is left switched on rather than risk switching yours") end -- debugc alone would not do: it writes to the editor's error console, which is -- hidden until the player goes looking for it, and is dropped entirely if the -- editor was never opened. The player-facing line is once per session, because -- arming runs again on every reconnect. function BaseUI.reportDeadChatGate(gate) debugc("[ Mudlet UI ] chat capture gate \"" .. gate .. "\" did not come up, so those lines will not be captured") if BaseUI.warnedDeadChatGate then return end BaseUI.warnedDeadChatGate = true cecho("\n[ Mudlet UI ] Part of the chat capture is switched off, so some chat may not appear here - type baseui for options.\n") end function BaseUI.disarmChatTriggers() if BaseUI.chatTreeShared() then BaseUI.reportSharedChatTree() return end disableTrigger(chatTree) end function BaseUI.chatTriggersArmed() for _, gate in ipairs(chatGates) do if not gateArmed(gate) then return false end end return true end -- vitals from plain text, for games that offer no protocol at all. Only -- self-sufficient shapes may drive a gauge: a labelled cur/max pair, a -- labelled percentage, or a labelled score-screen line - current-only -- prompts never invent a maximum. kind = "bare" rows exist to recognise -- those current-only prompts: they update currents once a maximum is known -- and arm the one-time auto-"score" request, nothing more. gated rows only -- go live after matching on three separate lines (prompts recur; chat -- mentions do not); score-screen rows are trusted on first sight because a -- score may only ever be shown once, and each one is anchored to line -- structure only a score screen has; windowed rows have no anchor at all -- and are trusted only for a few seconds after a "score" command really -- went to the game. -- two disambiguation lookbehinds recur below. On label-after shapes, -- numberFirstGuard keeps the numbers of a label-first reading from being -- claimed by the NEXT label ("HP: 523/600 MP: ..." must not read as -- 523/600 mp). On label-first shapes, labelFirstGuard keeps a label that -- closes a label-after reading from opening a new one ("87%hp 80%m" must -- not read as hp 80). Aligned tables pad with runs of spaces, and PCRE -- lookbehinds cannot be variable-length, so each guard spells out the run -- lengths (up to 8) as fixed-length alternatives. local numberFirstGuard = [=[(? 0 and max < maxSaneVital and current <= max * maxOverhealFactor then reading = { stat = pattern.stat, kind = pattern.kind, current = current, max = max } end elseif pattern.kind == "percent" and first then local percent = tonumber(first) if percent and percent <= 100 then reading = { stat = pattern.stat, kind = pattern.kind, percent = percent } end elseif pattern.kind == "bare" and first then local current = tonumber(first) if current and current < maxSaneVital then reading = { stat = pattern.stat, kind = pattern.kind, current = current } end end if reading then reading.pattern = index reading.gated = pattern.gated reading.windowed = pattern.windowed table.insert(readings, reading) end end return readings end function BaseUI.scoreWindowOpen() return BaseUI.scoreWindowUntil ~= nil and getEpoch() < BaseUI.scoreWindowUntil end -- lastChatLine keeps a line the chat layer routed out of the vitals layer; the -- refresh after applyVitals is because building the dock rewraps the buffer and -- renumbers lines, which would otherwise leave the marker on an unrelated line function BaseUI.onVitalsLine() local lineNumber = getLineNumber() if lineNumber == BaseUI.lastVitalsLine or lineNumber == BaseUI.lastChatLine then return end BaseUI.lastVitalsLine = lineNumber local updates = {} local windowOpen = BaseUI.scoreWindowOpen() for _, reading in ipairs(BaseUI.parseVitalsLine(line)) do local live = true if reading.windowed then live = windowOpen elseif reading.gated then local seen = (BaseUI.shapeSightings[reading.pattern] or 0) + 1 BaseUI.shapeSightings[reading.pattern] = seen live = seen >= 3 end if live then if reading.kind == "bare" then BaseUI.maybeRequestScore() end local update = updates[reading.stat] or {} update.current = reading.current or update.current update.max = reading.max or update.max update.percent = reading.percent or update.percent updates[reading.stat] = update end end if next(updates) then BaseUI.applyVitals("prompt", updates) -- building the dock resizes the main window, which can renumber lines; -- refresh the marker so other patterns on this same line stay deduplicated BaseUI.lastVitalsLine = getLineNumber() end end -- applyVitals discards prompt readings once a protocol holds the lock, so the -- plain-text layer is pure per-line cost from then on function BaseUI.structuredVitalsOwnGauges() return BaseUI.vitalsLock >= sourceRanks.msdp end function BaseUI.createVitalsTriggers() if BaseUI.dormant() or BaseUI.structuredVitalsOwnGauges() or next(BaseUI.vitalsTriggerIds) then return end BaseUI.vitalsTriggerIds = { tempRegexTrigger(BaseUI.vitalsPrefilter, BaseUI.onVitalsLine) } end function BaseUI.killVitalsTriggers() for _, id in ipairs(BaseUI.vitalsTriggerIds) do killTrigger(id) end BaseUI.vitalsTriggerIds = {} end -- last rung of the ladder: a game whose prompt only carries currents gets -- asked for its score screen - once per session, visibly, and only when no -- protocol has offered vitals and no maximum is known yet. The score output -- is picked up by the always-on score-screen shapes; if it teaches us -- nothing, that is the end of it - no retry, no error. function BaseUI.maybeRequestScore() if BaseUI.scoreRequested or BaseUI.sawGmcpVitals or BaseUI.sawMsdpVitals then return end local hp = BaseUI.vitalsData.hp if hp and (hp.max or hp.percent) then return end local _, _, connected = getConnectionInfo() if not connected then return end BaseUI.scoreRequested = true send("score") cecho("\n[ Mudlet UI ] Sent \"score\" once to size your gauges - type baseui to adjust.\n") end -- whenever a "score" command actually goes to the game - ours above, or the -- player typing it - the next few seconds of output ARE the score screen, -- so the anchorless windowed shapes may be trusted for that long.
